Mold-Tek Packaging: Guidance - - Concall Update

• Management is aiming for a full-year EBITDA per kg of INR 44-45, exceeding the initial target of INR 42-43, driven by consolidation benefits and improved efficiencies.

• The company projects the Paint segment's contribution to overall revenue to decrease from the current 50% (volume-wise) to around 40% over the next three to four years.

• Food and FMCG are expected to grow at an 18-20% CAGR, while Pharma is projected for a 40-50% CAGR over the next three to four years, with a Pharma revenue target of INR 50-55 crores for the current year.

• Overall volume growth for the full year is targeted at 10-12%, with 10% still considered achievable, and Paint volumes are expected to grow in the 10-15% range.

• CapEx for FY27 is projected at INR 90 crores, including INR 25-30 crores for Pharma, and the company plans for 10-12% annual capacity additions.

• For FY '27, revenue is projected to be INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores, with PAT ranging from INR300 crores to INR325 crores.

• PAT growth for FY '27 is expected to be maintained or rise by only about 10% due to a one-time tax burden in Q1 FY '27 from the One91 Thaltej land sale.

• Lease rentals from Million Minds will commence in Q4 FY '27, with full-year rentals expected in FY '28, potentially exceeding INR75 crores.

• The company prefers to provide guidance year-on-year rather than for multiple years due to market changes.

Nitin Gadkari moves Bombay High Court over alleged misinformation on E20 ethanol policy

Union Minister Nitin Gadkari has approached the Bombay High Court against social media posts that allegedly link him and his family to business gains from India’s E20 ethanol blending programme.

According to the civil suit, the disputed content includes posts, deepfake images, and videos claiming that Gadkari and his family benefited financially from the ethanol blending initiative.

The petition argues that these allegations are false and notes that the E20 ethanol blending policy is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, not by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways headed by Gadkari.

The Bombay High Court has permitted Gadkari to proceed with a civil suit against Meta, other social media platforms, and unidentified individuals or entities allegedly responsible for creating and disseminating the defamatory content. The case seeks legal remedies against the spread of what Gadkari describes as misinformation targeting him and his family.

The Company has opened its 53rd retail store at Karanja Road, Uran, Raigad, further strengthening its retail footprint across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR). The new store reflects Patel Retail's continued focus on expanding into high-potential suburban and emerging urban markets while bringing its neighbourhood retail format closer to customers.

Strategically located to serve Uran and the surrounding areas, the new outlet is expected to enhance customer accessibility and convenience. The expansion aligns with the Company's long-term strategy of strengthening its presence in key markets through a steadily growing retail network.

With every new store, Patel Retail continues to make quality groceries, daily essentials, household products and value-driven offerings more accessible to customers. The Company remains focused on identifying strategic locations that support sustainable growth while delivering a reliable and convenient shopping experience to local communities.

Every large gas turbine maker in world is booked out for years, because AI data centres need power faster than grids can supply. 

GE Vernova alone has more than 100 gigawatts of gas orders waiting, Bottleneck is not turbine assembly itself, it is castings, means parts made by pouring molten metal into moulds, that go inside them. Indo-MIM grows that casting line near 50% a year. 

Anyone buying this IPO owns small piece of that power shortage

Defence gives Indo-MIM 18.7% of revenue, but much of it means firing mechanism parts for American gun makers, not missiles That market has not grown since 2020, and dealer shelves across United States stay full. 

Gross margin, which is money left after paying for raw material, fell from 86% to 79% last year partly because this defence share shrank. Highest earning corner of business rides on American shoppers, and few people pricing this IPO have noticed

Quietly, Indo-MIM built second business at home. Its metal powder, tooling and traded goods sales jumped from 94 crore rupees in FY24 to 665 crore in FY26, almost entirely inside India, lifting that share of revenue from 3% to 16%. 

Powder earns thinner margin than finished parts, which explains part of last year profit dip. Selling powder locally also puts it inside India young 3D printing supply chain

🚨MASSIVE ACHIEVEMENT BY INDIA: India Has Buit Indigenous 1200 kV Ultra High Voltage Transformer, Even US Doesn't Own Such Technology 

India has achieved a major milestone in power transmission technology with the successful design, manufacturing and commissioning of its first indigenous 1200 kV Ultra High Voltage (UHV) AC transformer. Developed by BHEL through in-house research and development, the transformer has been installed and commissioned at Power Grid Corporation's 1200 kV National Test Station in Bina, Madhya Pradesh.

The transformer has now been successfully integrated into the power grid, proving its performance under real operating conditions. The transition from laboratory development to field deployment marks a significant technological leap.

Ultra-high voltage transmission is one of the most demanding areas of electrical engineering. While generating electricity has become increasingly efficient with modern technologies, transmitting massive amounts of power across thousands of kilometres with minimal losses remains a far greater challenge. This is precisely where ultra-high voltage transformers play a critical role.

The importance of this breakthrough is particularly significant as India rapidly expands its renewable energy capacity. Large solar parks in Rajasthan and Gujarat, wind projects along the southern coastline, hydropower plants in the Himalayas and future nuclear facilities are often located far from major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. 

With this successful commissioning, India joins an exclusive group of nations like China that have demonstrated advanced capabilities in 1200 kV ultra-high voltage transmission technology. Even USA has 700-800 KV transformer

Fineotex Chemical Limited Delivers Robust Q1 FY27 Performance; 

Total Income, EBITDA and Net Profit Surge 164.94%, 134.70% and 92.67% YoY

📌**Q1 FY27 Consolidated Key Financial Highlights**

* Total Income at ₹386.72 crore, up 164.94% YoY

**EBITDA** at ₹59.14 crore, up 134.70% YoY

* EBITDA Margin at 15.70%

* Net Profit at ₹48.21 crore, up 92.67% YoY

* Net Profit Margin at 12.80%

*EBITDA excludes Other Income

📌 **Key Performance Highlights**

* Consolidated Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) stood at approximately 33.06% in Q1 FY27.

* Consolidated business volume increased by approximately 130.84% YoY in Q1 FY27.

📌 Key Operational Highlights

* Expanded CrudeChem Technology's Texas manufacturing capacity by 150 million pounds per annum, increasing the total installed capacity from 200 million pounds to 350 million pounds annually.

* Strengthened the Company's North American manufacturing footprint to cater to the growing demand for specialty chemicals across domestic and international markets.

- EBITDA margin at 16.7%.
- Margin missed estimate by 75 bps.

**Sona BLW | Citi Raises Target Price**

**Brokerage Update**
- Citi maintained **Buy** rating.
- Target price raised to **₹830**.
- Q1 results exceeded estimates.
- Revenue growth beat expectations.

**Management Outlook**
- Positive demand outlook maintained.
- Strong growth in EU hybrid market.
- Indian EV demand remains robust.
- Targets **10x revenue growth** over 10 years.

**Growth Drivers**
- Expansion into railway business.
- Two Denso JVs strengthen portfolio.
- Expanding presence in East markets.
- New robotics and Physical AI vertical.

**Order Book & Margins**
- Order book at **₹24,000 crore**.
- Increased **₹300 crore QoQ**.
- Margins impacted by commodity costs.
- Higher labour costs also weighed.
- Cost trends improved during June.
- Commodity costs passed through with lag.

**Impact**
- **Positive**.
- Strong revenue performance.
- Healthy long-term growth roadmap.
- Robust order book supports visibility.
- Margin pressure expected to ease.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Citi maintained its Buy rating on Sona BLW and raised the target price to ₹830 after a stronger-than-expected Q1. The brokerage highlighted robust demand in EU hybrids and Indian EVs, a record ₹24,000 crore order book, and multiple long-term growth drivers including railways, Denso joint ventures, and robotics, while expecting margin pressures from commodity costs to moderate over time.**

**Sona BLW | Nomura Raises Target Price**

**Brokerage Update**
- Nomura maintained **Buy** rating.
- Target price raised to **₹848**.
- Earlier target price **₹720**.
- Q1 results broadly in line.

**Growth Drivers**
- Denso JV opens global 4W motor opportunity.
- Sona strong in electric motors.
- Denso brings controller expertise.
- JV targets global EV market.

**Strategic Highlights**
- "Sona 2.0" targets **10x growth** by FY35.
- Entered robotics and Physical AI.
- Robotics order book at **₹800 crore**.

**Industry Opportunity**
- Addressable market seen at **₹20,000 crore** by 2030.
- Significant long-term expansion potential.
- Asset turnover targeted at **8x** in 2W.
- Asset turnover targeted at **11–12x** in 4W.

**Impact**
- **Positive**.
- Target price upgraded.
- Global EV opportunity expands.
- New robotics business adds growth.
- Long-term outlook strengthens.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Nomura maintained its Buy rating on Sona BLW and raised the target price to ₹848 from ₹720. The brokerage believes the Denso joint venture significantly expands the company's global EV motor opportunity, while its "Sona 2.0" strategy, entry into robotics and Physical AI, and ambitious FY35 growth plans strengthen the long-term investment case.**

**Infosys | Nomura Maintains Buy**

**Brokerage Update**
- Nomura maintained **Buy** rating.
- Target price at **₹1,290**.
- Q1FY27 revenue missed expectations.
- Weakness driven by client-specific issues.

**Key Observations**
- FY27 organic growth guidance cut.
- Mid-point lowered by **170 bps**.
- FY27 margin guidance unchanged.
- EBIT margin guidance at **20–22%**.

**Management Update**
- CEO transition remains a key monitorable.
- Smooth succession execution in focus.

**Valuation View**
- Trading at attractive valuations.
- Valued at **13x FY28F EPS**.
- FY28F EPS estimated at **₹80.4**.

**Impact**
- **Positive**.
- Revenue outlook weakened.
- Margin guidance maintained.
- Attractive valuations support optimism.
- Buy rating retained.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Nomura maintained its Buy rating on Infosys with a target price of ₹1,290. While Q1FY27 revenue and FY27 growth guidance disappointed due to client-specific issues, stable margin guidance, attractive valuations and confidence in a smooth CEO transition support the brokerage's positive long-term view.**

**Infosys | CLSA Maintains Outperform**

**Brokerage Update**
- CLSA maintained **Outperform** rating.
- Target price at **₹1,109**.
- Q1FY27 revenue growth disappointed.
- FY27 guidance cut below expectations.
- EBIT margin exceeded estimates.
- Order book remained steady.

**Key Positives**
- Margin performance remained strong.
- Healthy order book supports outlook.
- Leadership concerns partially addressed.
- AI strategy execution confidence improved.

**Management Update**
- Ashiss Kumar Dash appointed CEO-designate.
- To become CEO from **1 April 2027**.
- Currently heads the EURS vertical.
- Associated with Infosys for **31 years**.
- First insider, non-founder CEO in history.
- Reflects Infosys' meritocratic culture.

**Impact**
- **Positive**.
- Strong margins offset weak growth.
- Stable deal pipeline reassuring.
- Leadership transition viewed favourably.
- AI execution confidence improves.

**Key Takeaway**
- **CLSA maintained its Outperform rating on Infosys with a target price of ₹1,109. Although Q1FY27 revenue growth and the FY27 guidance cut were disappointing, stronger-than-expected margins, a stable order book and the appointment of long-time insider Ashiss Kumar Dash as CEO-designate improved confidence in the company's long-term execution amid AI-led disruption.**

**Infosys | Citi Maintains Neutral**

**Brokerage Update**
- Citi maintained **Neutral** rating.
- Target price at **₹1,065**.
- Q1 organic revenue remained flattish QoQ.
- Margins and deal TCV were healthy.

**Key Observations**
- FY27 guidance includes Optimum Health acquisition.
- Organic guidance midpoint cut by **170+ bps**.
- TTM deal TCV grew **30% YoY**.
- Headcount increased around **1% YoY**.
- Management flagged uncertain macro environment.
- Discretionary spending remains cautious.
- Competitive intensity remains elevated.

**Management Update**
- Ashiss Kumar Dash named CEO designate.
- Currently Global Head of EURS.

**Earnings Impact**
- FY27E EPS cut by **1–2%**.
- FY28E EPS cut by **1–2%**.

**Impact**
- **Neutral**.
- Organic growth outlook weakened.
- Strong deal wins provide support.
- Margins remained resilient.
- Earnings estimates revised lower.

**Key Takeaway**
- **Citi maintained a Neutral rating on Infosys with a target price of ₹1,065. While Q1 margins and deal wins remained healthy, the brokerage lowered earnings estimates after the company sharply reduced its organic growth outlook amid macro uncertainty, cautious discretionary spending and intense competition.**

**Infosys | JPM Downgrades to Neutral**

**Brokerage Update**
- JPM downgraded stock to **Neutral**.
- Target price set at **₹1,050**.
- Q1 revenue missed expectations sharply.
- FY27 revenue guidance cut again.

**Key Reasons**
- Weak demand impacting growth.
- AI-driven pricing deflation continues.
- Daimler contract challenges persist.
- EURS contract termination impacted growth.
- Strong deal wins not converting into revenue.
- FY27 organic growth guidance cut to **-0.2% to 1.3%**.

**Margins & Management**
- Margins broadly in line.
- Margin defence needed through FY27.
- Ashiss Kumar Dash named next CEO.
- Leadership transition over next nine months.
- Smooth succession expected.

**Impact**
- **Negative**.
- Consecutive guidance downgrades.
- Growth outlook weakened materially.
- Revenue conversion remains soft.
- Leadership change viewed positively.

**Key Takeaway**
- **JPM downgraded Infosys to Neutral with a target price of ₹1,050 after another sharp revenue miss and a second consecutive cut in FY27 guidance. Weak demand, AI-led pricing pressure and contract-related issues have hurt growth, although the planned CEO transition to Ashiss Kumar Dash is expected to provide leadership continuity.**

**Infosys | HSBC Downgrades to Hold**

**Brokerage Update**
- HSBC downgraded stock to **Hold**.
- Target price cut to **₹1,110**.
- Earlier target price **₹1,340**.

**Key Reasons**
- Infosys lowered FY27 growth guidance.
- Cut larger than market expectations.
- Near-term business outlook remains weak.
- Relative valuations appear inexpensive.

**Management Update**
- Ashiss Kumar Dash appointed new CEO.
- Will assume role from **1 April 2027**.
- Internal leadership transition announced.

**Impact**
- **Negative**.
- Lower growth guidance disappoints.
- Target price reduced significantly.
- Weak near-term earnings outlook.

**Key Takeaway**
- **HSBC downgraded Infosys to Hold and cut its target price to ₹1,110 after the company reduced its FY27 growth guidance more than expected. While valuations are becoming attractive and a new CEO has been appointed, the brokerage expects weak business performance over the coming quarters.**
